title: Positivity of the Mills ratio
statement: Let $\\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian density and $\\Phi$ its cumulative distribution function, and define $R(t)=\\Phi(t)(-t)/\\varphi(t)$ for real $t$. For every real $t<0$, one has $0<R(t)$.
replaced: Let $\varphi(x)=e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}$, $\Phi(t)=\int_{-\infty}^{t}\varphi(x)\,dx$, and $R(t)=\Phi(t)(-t)/\varphi(t)$ for $t\in\mathbb R$. For every real $t<0$, one has $0<R(t)$.
